abstract:
Anti-SSA/Ro antibodies are a hallmark of Sjögren's disease (SjD), but the respective roles of anti-TRIM21/Ro52 and anti-TROVE2/Ro60 antibodies remain unclear. We investigated whether distinct anti-TRIM21/Ro52 and/or anti-TROVE2/Ro60 serological profiles are associated with differences in clinical phenotype, systemic activity, patient-reported symptoms, and lymphoma risk over time.
Patients from the prospective multicenter ASSESS cohort were stratified accordingly as Ro52-/Ro60-, Ro60+ only, Ro52+ only, or Ro52+/Ro60+. Baseline clinical, biological, and immunological parameters were compared across groups. Patient-reported symptoms (ESSPRI) and systemic disease activity (ESSDAI) were evaluated over 5 years using age-adjusted mixed-effects models. ESSDAI domains and lymphoma cases were also assessed.
Among 365 patients, 123 were Ro52-/Ro60-, 25 Ro52+, 23 Ro60+, and 194 Ro52+/Ro60+. At baseline, both Ro52+ and Ro52+/Ro60+ patients displayed the highest levels of markers associated with systemic disease activity, including β2-microglobulin, positivity of rheumatoid factor and IFN-α levels. Conversely, Ro60+ patients resembled immunonegative patients. Baseline ESSPRI was higher in Ro52-/Ro60- compared with Ro52+/Ro60+ patients, but this difference faded over time, due to the ESSPRI worsening in Ro52+/Ro60+ patients. ESSDAI scores were consistently higher in Ro52+ and Ro52+/Ro60+ patients compared to other groups. Domain analysis indicated that biological, articular, hematological and glandular domains could contribute to these differences. Lymphoma events were recorded in 7/116 (6.0%) Ro52-/Ro60-, 5/24 Ro52+ (20.8%), 0/19 Ro60+, and 17/189 Ro52+/Ro60+ (9.0%) patients.
Anti-TRIM21/Ro52 and anti-TROVE2/Ro60 are linked to distinct SjD phenotypes. Anti-TRIM21/Ro52 positivity is associated with greater systemic disease activity, whereas anti-TROVE2/Ro60, although useful for diagnosis, have a limited relationship with disease expression.
